## labs/nvidia/cosmos-drive-dreams

Cosmos Drive Dreams - Generates synthetic multi-view autonomous-vehicle video and LiDAR from HD map, bounding box, and LiDAR conditions.

Status: blocked-platform. Install: none. Artifact: container-image. Arm64: absent. GB10: unsupported. Comfy shape: host-cli.
Input: HD map, bounding boxes, and LiDAR conditions
Output: multi-view synthetic AV video plus LiDAR
Licenses: code Apache-2.0. Weights NVIDIA Open Model License (inherited from the Cosmos cards). Commercial use permitted.
Footprint: 40 GB VRAM, 80 GB disk. Weights: nvidia/Cosmos-Transfer1-7B-Sample-AV/base_model.pt@28.95.
Artifact ref: nvcr.io/nvidia/cosmos
Upstream: https://github.com/nv-tlabs/Cosmos-Drive-Dreams
Also: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Cosmos-Transfer1-7B-Sample-AV
Sources: https://github.com/nv-tlabs/Cosmos-Drive-Dreams

Nothing in this graph touches the GPU. The row's work runs outside the Comfy process through the operator CLI, so the App claims no occupancy and stops no heavy job: the one-heavy-job rule is the CLI's to enforce, next to the heavy confirm and the headroom preflight.

Operator verbs (host shell):
  bazelisk run //:manage -- nvidia-lab status
  bazelisk run //:manage -- nvidia-lab plan cosmos-drive-dreams

Canvas:
1. Preflight prints whether this Spark could run the row today - the catalog row, an aarch64 host, the binary that row's install kind needs, and the artifact ref.
2. The verdict card prints the blocking reason and the sentence that would reopen the row.
3. The tier table prints all 18 rows with their status and licenses.

Gate notes: The license is workable but the Cosmos 1 upstream it needs ships x86_64 NGC images and prebuilt CUDA wheels, so nothing resolves inside this aarch64 image. Its input domain is autonomous-vehicle sensor conditions, which no lane in this stack produces.
Reopen: Upstream Cosmos publishes linux_aarch64 wheels or an arm64 container that runs on GB10.
Verify: bazelisk test //tests:bats_nvidia_lab_test

Occupancy: none - stop nothing GPU. One GB10 job.
